OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@jakarta.validation.constraints.NotBlank"
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create it is normalized to
            E.164 form: spaces, dashes and brackets are stripped; a leading '+' and
            country code are kept when present, otherwise '+61' is assumed and a
            single leading '0' is dropped from the national digits. The result must
            have 8 to 15 digits after the '+'. The normalized E.164 value is stored
            and returned (e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678').
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          x-field-extra-annotation: "@org.springframework.samples.petclinic.rest.validation.TelephoneValidation"
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The email address of the pet owner. Optional; when present it must be a
            syntactically valid address. It is stored and returned lower-cased.
          type: string
          format: email
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, in ISO 'YYYY-MM-DD' format.
            Optional on create; when omitted it defaults to the server's current
            date. Once set it is stored and returned unchanged.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        sharesHousehold:

## Summary

I introduced address normalization that is applied whenever an owner is created, mirroring the existing email/telephone normalization conventions in this Spring Boot app.

### Changes

**`model/Owner.java`**
- Added a canonical `normalizeAddress(String)` static method (the single source of truth): trims and collapses internal whitespace, upper-cases, and expands common street-type abbreviations as whole tokens (`ST`→`STREET`, `RD`→`ROAD`, `AVE`→`AVENUE`). It is null-safe and idempotent (a normalized address normalizes to itself), backed by an `ADDRESS_ABBREVIATIONS` map.
- `setAddress(...)` now stores the normalized form, so every persistence path (the MapStruct mapper on create, and the hand-copied update path) stores and returns the canonical value — matching how `setEmail` already normalizes.
- `householdId(...)` now derives the address component via `normalizeAddress` instead of `normalizeHousehold`, so the shared household id uses the normalized form.

**`service/ClinicServiceImpl.java`**
- `assertHouseholdIsUnique(...)` now compares addresses via `Owner.normalizeAddress` on both the candidate and existing owners, so duplicate-household detection uses the normalized form (robust even against non-normalized seed data).

### Behaviour notes
- The required-field check rejects an address that is blank after normalization: the `OwnerFields.address` DTO constraint (`@NotBlank`) already rejects whitespace-only input with `400`, and whitespace-only is the only input that normalizes to blank — so this is consistent with the normalized form.
- The three acceptance tests pass: `  12  main  st ` → `12 MAIN STREET`, `7 elm ave` → `7 ELM AVENUE`, and `   ` → `400`.

Full suite: `Tests run: 3, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.
